topology: Three-router area0 P2P triangle with PC1 behind R1, PC2 behind R2 and SRV1 behind R3. Direct R1–R3 transit cost5 plus LAN1 gives service cost6; backup R1–R2–R3 costs21. PC2 server path costs11. Practice begins with R1 Gi0/2 in area1 while R3 Gi0/2 remains area0, so working backup traffic hides the primary fault.
implemented: Eighteenth ENARSI Layer3 Technologies entry with independent practice/completed documents, six-row addressing/cost plan, staged instructions, executable reference/verification commands and current-origin/path/query permalinks. Existing engine, UI layout, artwork and terminal styling are preserved.

Initial diagnosis requires three accepted requests and parent-linked replies in four host/server directions, using the actual R2 backup for PC1 and the independent R2–R3 control for PC2. The primary pair is not Full despite working pings; area0 repair must restore direct cost6 forwarding.

Live OSPF checks require intended interface activation, configured and operational router IDs, explicit costs, passive LANs, P2P transits, default timers, matching lab authentication keys, MTU1500 and no mtu-ignore. All three Full pairs, three received router LSAs with LAN prefixes, intra-area O routes at AD110 and exact next hops/costs6/11 are required.

Actual four-way host traffic and a complete PC1 HTTP200 service body are observed after repair. Traffic goals correlate accepted requests, delivered parent-linked replies and expected router egresses; configuring routes or reading show output cannot fabricate the observations.

Hello/dead mismatch, passive transit and wrong authentication key each remove the primary Full relationship while physical links stay up and backup traffic remains working. Each exercise requires actual bidirectional PC1 backup requests and independent bidirectional PC2 control requests before restoration and fresh four-way primary traffic.

MTU1400 on R1 primary produces actual local ExStart and a database-description MTU diagnostic, with cost21 backup routes in both directions. R1 must return to MTU1500 and the direct Full pair; mtu-ignore may permit forwarding but cannot satisfy intended health or recovery. MTU state checks target the local R1 state; peer displays may be asymmetric during the modeled negotiation.

Removing only R3 server-LAN OSPF activation keeps every transit Full but withdraws the /24 from remote routes/received LSAs. Both PCs must experience actual No route drops while PC1 and PC2 exchange successful control probes. Restoring the LAN advertisement needs fresh replies in all four service directions.

Increasing only R1 primary cost to30 preserves all Full pairs but makes forward service requests use R2 at21 while reverse server requests stay on the direct R3–R1 path at6. Actual asymmetric requests and independent PC2 traffic must be observed, then cost5 and fresh symmetric primary traffic restored.

Six live and nine historical criteria produce practice0/15, original diagnosis1/15, baseline9/15 and full15/15. Per-attempt configuration/route epochs reject stale traffic and config-only toggles. YAML retains earned history while dropping runtime; new practice starts fresh. Rendered config replay uses a real IOS OSPF process restart to apply router IDs that appear after interface activation, and saved reload repairs unsaved timer changes.
scope: IOS IPv4 single-area OSPF troubleshooting with a deliberately mismatched primary area, P2P transit, timer/passive/key/MTU/advertisement/cost faults and actual simulated control/data-plane delivery. No new engine commands were required. No fresh CML capture, complete bilateral RFC state/timing equivalence, wire-format interoperability, cryptographic MD5 digest generation, multi-area type/filter exercise, duplicate-router-ID incident or OSPFv3 exercise is claimed. Authentication uses the existing modeled key compatibility behavior.
